description: One cell of a Luci network: a ramp that runs from 0 to 1, fires a pulse on all four sides when it gets there and has its phase knocked about by pulses from its neighbours

params.text: Sends the ramp back to the start and fires the cell's pulse

inputs.text: A pulse here multiplies the cell's phase by the influence setting, which pulls the ramp back towards its start
Any voltage other than zero here throws the ramp to a random position and holds the audio output at 0V for that sample
Sets the cell's rate at a volt per octave from a base of about an eighth of a hertz; with nothing patched the ramp takes about eight seconds
Sets how much a neighbour's pulse moves this cell's phase, 0V leaving the phase at zero after a pulse and 10V leaving it almost untouched

outputs.text: Carries the ramp itself, -5V to 5V, rising from the bottom to the top over one cycle
Goes to 1V for one sample when the ramp reaches the top, for patching into a neighbouring cell

notes: with nothing patched the cell runs on its own, putting out a rising ramp about once every eight seconds; the frequency, influence and randomize jacks are what the Luci control modules are for
the four side inputs are not edge detected: any voltage other than zero counts as a pulse, so a held high gate pulls the phase back on every sample
all four trigger outputs carry exactly the same pulse, and the pulse is 1V rather than the usual 10V, which is what the other Luci modules expect
the influence input comes up unpatched at 0V, which makes every incoming pulse reset the cell's phase to zero rather than nudge it

inputs.0: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.3: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.4: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.5: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
